summary.text: 假 is conventionally analyzed as a phonosemantic compound: 亻 contributes a person-related meaning and 叚 supplies a sound cue. The character is used for “false” and “borrow,” but the evidence here does not establish which sense came first or a semantic path between them.

formation.text: The conventional analysis combines the positional side form 亻 of 人 with phonetic 叚. A competing proposal treats 人 as an addition distinguishing 假 from 叚 in Qin-period writing; that proposal concerns why the graph was differentiated, while the conventional analysis assigns 亻 a semantic role. Their accounts do not settle the character’s earliest sense.

components.text: 亻 is the positional side form of 人, and the conventional analysis assigns it a person-related semantic contribution in 假. A proposal that 人 was added to distinguish 假 from 叚 concerns the graph’s formation, not the relationship between 亻 and 人.
叚 is conventionally analyzed as 假’s phonetic component. Accounts of 叚’s bronze forms concern that character and do not establish a graphic sequence for 假.

sound_limitation.text: The sound comparisons support particular readings, but do not show that the relationship applies to every reading of 假.

sound.text: Modern Mandarin data list both 叚 and 假 with the reading jiǎ; 叚 is also listed with xiá. This current match alone does not establish their ancient sound relationship.
In Baxter–Sagart Old Chinese notation, 叚 and 假 in the “borrow; false” reading are both reconstructed *Cə.kˤraʔ. The same dataset gives another reconstruction for a different reading of 假.

history.text: A scholarly account reports 叚 in excavated pre-Qin texts and 假 in Qin-period documents. It interprets a document dated to 221 BCE as distinguishing 叚 for lending from 假 for borrowing, and proposes that 人 was added to differentiate the written form. This is an interpretation of the textual evidence, not an inspected manuscript facsimile.
Later texts are reported to mix the spellings 叚 and 假. The available evidence does not trace a dated sequence of 假’s graphic changes through later script styles.

An account of 叚’s bronze forms describes 爪, 又, and 石 as graphic elements and lists uses read as “blessing,” “fault,” interrogative words, and others. These descriptions concern 叚; they do not establish an evolutionary path for 假.

uncertainties.text: The conventional analysis assigns 亻 a semantic role and 叚 a phonetic role; another proposal treats 人 as a differentiating addition. The accounts do not resolve how that proposed graphic differentiation relates to the conventional component analysis.
The proposed development from “borrow” through “simulate” to “false” is disputed; the cited accounts do not establish a dated bridge between “borrow” and “false.”
A historical sound comparison is available for one reading in Baxter–Sagart’s reconstruction, but the evidence does not show that it applies to every reading of 假.

senses.text: 假 is glossed as “not true,” and a cited classical example uses it to mean “false” or “not so.” The example’s date and status as an earliest attestation are not securely established here.

senses.period: classical text; composition and attestation dating unresolved
senses.text: A cited classical example uses 假 for borrowing a passage. A scholarly account interprets Qin-period writing as distinguishing 假 for borrowing from 叚 for lending; this reported distinction does not establish that “borrow” preceded “false” as a meaning of 假.

senses.period: historical and current; first attestation unresolved
senses.text: Textual examples record temporary or acting uses, and modern definitions include “vacation.” Their dates and relationship to “borrow” or “false” are not established.

limitations.text: The cited senses establish neither their relative chronology nor a continuous semantic development. In particular, the proposed path from borrowing through simulation to falsehood remains disputed.

overview.text: 假 combines a person-related element with 叚 as a sound cue. It is used for “false” and “borrow,” but the evidence does not establish which meaning came first or how they are connected.

components.text: 亻 is the side form of 人; in the conventional analysis, it contributes a person-related meaning.
叚 is conventionally treated as the sound component; the comparisons shown support particular readings, not every use of 假.

relationships.text: In the conventional analysis of 假, 亻 contributes a person-related meaning; a competing account treats 人 as a differentiating addition.
The conventional analysis assigns 叚 the sound role. A Baxter–Sagart Old Chinese reconstruction lists matching forms for 叚 and one reading of 假; this does not establish the role for every reading.
